column1: What's the scoping difference between let, const, and var?
column2: let and const are block-scoped. var is function-scoped (or global), which can leak values outside the expected block.
=== compares value and type with no implicit conversion. == performs type coercion, producing unexpected results (e.g. "1" == 1 is true).
var and function declarations are "hoisted" to the top of their scope before execution — var becomes undefined until its assignment line, while function is fully available.

column1: What's the "this" behavior difference between a declared function and an arrow function?
column2: A declared function has dynamic "this" (depends on how it's called). An arrow function inherits "this" from the lexical scope where it was created.

column1: What's the difference between null and undefined?
column2: undefined is the default value of something not yet initialized. null is an absence of value assigned intentionally by the programmer.

column1: What is a closure? Give a short example.
column2: A function that "remembers" variables from the scope where it was created, even after that scope has ended. Example: a counter function that keeps an internal variable between calls.

column1: What's the difference between Promise and async/await?
column2: async/await is syntactic sugar over Promise — same underlying mechanism, but with more readable, sequential-looking syntax (no chained .then()).

column1: What's the difference between map and forEach?
column2: map returns a new, transformed array. forEach only iterates and returns nothing useful (returns undefined).

column1: What is reduce used for in arrays?
column2: A generic tool that accumulates a single value from all array items (sum, grouping, transforming into an object, etc).

column1: What's the difference between split, slice, and substring on strings?
column2: split breaks a string into an array by a delimiter. slice extracts part of a string by index (accepts negative). substring is similar to slice but doesn't accept negative indexes.
Backtick strings (`) that allow direct variable interpolation with ${variable}, without manual concatenation.
Syntax that extracts values from an object or array directly into named variables, without accessing property by property.

column1: When should you use for...of instead of a classic for loop?
column2: When you just need to iterate values of an iterable (array, string) without manually controlling the index.

column1: When does a nested loop signal a complexity problem?
column2: When it produces unnecessary O(n²) — a signal to look for a data structure (e.g. hash map) that avoids the second pass.

column1: What do the && and || operators do in short-circuit evaluation?
column2: && returns the first falsy value or the last value. || returns the first truthy value or the last value — used for default values and short conditional checks.
